title: Is a '10% flat' loan a 10% loan?
hook: A loan is quoted at 10% flat. What yearly rate is that on what you owe?

knows: a loan charges interest and is repaid in monthly instalments (first-payment-mostly-interest)
doesNotKnow: that a flat rate charges interest on the original amount for the whole term, even after half of it has been repaid, so the true yearly rate on what you actually owe is nearly double

misconception: A 10% flat rate costs 10% a year, like any 10% loan.
objective: The learner can explain that a 10% flat rate on $10,000 over 2 years charges interest on the full $10,000 every month although the balance falls, so on what is actually owed the yearly rate is 18.2%, and a true 10% loan costs about half the interest ($1,075 vs $2,000).

claims.text: A flat 10% rate over 2 years on $10,000 charges $2,000 interest (10% of the full $10,000, both years), repaid as 24 payments of $500.
claims.source: Flat rule (stated on the card chip): interest = 10,000 × 0.10 × 2 = 2,000; (10,000 + 2,000) / 24 = 500. Demo.tsx loan('flat', 2). Brief: company/domains/briefs/economics.md #60.
claims.note: Derivation, re-run (artifacts/fact-check-wave-j/wj-econ-phys-math-geo/flat.mjs, copy of loan()): flat interest 10,000 x 0.10 x 2 = 2,000; payment (10,000 + 2,000)/24 = 500.00. Code path: the 'flat' milestone records only at the 2-year term, so the reveal's $2,000 is always this case.

claims.text: On what you actually owe, the flat 10% loan's true yearly rate is 18.2% (monthly rate 1.513%, times 12).
claims.source: Bisection on 10,000 = 500 × (1 − (1 + r)^−24) / r gives r = 1.5131% a month; 12 × r = 18.16%, shown as 18.2% (APR convention, monthly rate × 12; the stage readout is labelled 'True rate'). Demo.tsx solveRate(); builder node run 2026-10-14.
claims.note: Derivation: the lesson's bisection gives r = 1.5131% a month, and my independent Newton solve gives 1.51308%; 12 x r = 18.157%, shown as 18.2% (APR convention, labelled 'monthly rate, times 12' in the claim). For the record, the effective annual rate (1 + r)^12 - 1 is 19.75%; the question's options (10/14/18%) are unaffected. artifacts/fact-check-wave-j/wj-econ-phys-math-geo/flat.mjs.

claims.text: After 12 of the 24 flat payments, the balance still owed at that true rate is $5,449.
claims.source: Step b ← b × 1.015131 − 500 twelve times from 10,000: 5,449.31. Demo.tsx loan('flat', 2).bal[12]; drawn as the labelled dot on the staircase.
claims.note: Derivation: stepping b <- b(1 + r) - 500 twelve times from 10,000 gives 5,449.31; the stage dot and the reveal print $5,449. artifacts/fact-check-wave-j/wj-econ-phys-math-geo/flat.mjs.

claims.text: Under the flat rate the interest charged stays at $83 a month (10% of $10,000 over 12 months) for every month of the term, while the balance falls.
claims.source: 10,000 × 0.10 / 12 = 83.33 per month for all n months (flat rule). Demo.tsx loan().charged for mode 'flat'.
claims.note: Derivation: under the flat rule charged = 10,000 x 0.10 / 12 = 83.33 every month (loan().charged, first and last month both 83.33); the balance falls to 0 at month 24.

claims.text: A true 10% loan (10% APR, interest charged monthly on what is left) of $10,000 over 24 months has a payment of $461 ($461.45) and costs $1,075 ($1,074.78) in interest, about half of $2,000.
claims.note: Derivation, standard annuity: payment 461.45, interest 1,074.78 (24 x 461.45 - 10,000); 1,074.78 / 2,000 = 0.54, 'about half'. artifacts/fact-check-wave-j/wj-econ-phys-math-geo/flat.mjs.

claims.text: For 1 to 3 year terms the flat 10% loan's true rate stays between 17.9% and 18.2% (1 year: 17.97%, 2 years: 18.16%, 3 years: 17.92%); shown on the stage when the learner moves the term slider in flat mode.
claims.source: Same bisection with 12 × $916.67, 24 × $500, 36 × $361.11 (builder node run 2026-10-14). Demo.tsx solveRate().
claims.note: Derivation: 1 year 17.972% (shown 18.0%), 2 years 18.157% (18.2%), 3 years 17.918% (17.9%). The slider reaches only these three terms. artifacts/fact-check-wave-j/wj-econ-phys-math-geo/flat.mjs.

claims.text: The lesson is a made-up loan with level monthly payments and no fees; not a statement about any lender.
claims.source: Assumptions of Demo.tsx loan(); reveal's last sentence. Brief keeps claims about where flat (add-on) quotes are common out of learner text.
claims.note: Lesson rule, checked against the code: loan() has level payments and no fee term; the reveal says 'A made-up loan with level payments and no fees'.

recall.question: Two 2-year loans of $10,000: one '10% flat', one 10% charged on what you still owe. Which costs more interest?
options: The flat loan, by nearly double
They cost the same: both are 10%
The second loan, because interest is charged monthly
recall.why: A flat rate charges interest on the full amount for the whole term, even after much of it is repaid, so it costs about twice the interest of a true 10% loan.
